x: Kealey and Stroud were our hopes in the 100 yards match. The former finished second, with Stroud close up, fourth; but T.V.H. had first and third and so gained a two-points lead.

Williams is a young schoolmaster resident in London, and we have every hope that he will prove an addition to our cross-country strength. Kealey could not be caught by Kench in the 440 yards final, whilst the 100 yards handicap was taken by J.
Kealey, but Kealey had his reward for some consistent sprinting throughout the season in winning the 220 yards title. Alf Kench retained his 440 yards championship in a close finish with R.
All four clubs competed in the 4 x 300 yards and with Kealey running a fine third leg, Tom Scrimshaw went off with a lead over the Croydon runner.
In the fourth of the six events, held at the "Kinnaird" meeting, a relay 4 x 220 yards, were placed third, Stroud, Kealey, Pack and Basford forming our team.

Owing to the late appearance of Eddie Kealey, our team in the 4 x 100 yards was not at full strength; and in the circumstances they did well to finish third in a very close finish, with Croydon beating Mitcham for first place.

On May 25th, at the White City, was held the 4 x 220 yds. and we fielded a useful team in Kealey, Stroud, Mewes and Michael. Kealey elected to start for us, and drawing number 1 station, he was twice bumped very badly and so we lost any advantage which we might have had.
Epsom again beat Croydon for third place; and their half-milers are beginning to weld themselves into a useful team. We welcomed Eddie Kealey back into the active ranks for this meeting; while S.
We (the Belgrave Harriers) would also like to see some of the older members back in training, such as Messrs. Bone, Mewes, Kealey and Co. The Club has many promising juniors also.
